title: Match with Guards
concept: Add if guards to match arms to filter patterns with additional conditions beyond simple value matching.
why: Sometimes a pattern alone isn't enough — you need to check 'this value BUT only if some condition is true'. Guards give you that precision.
tips: `variable if condition` — variable captures the value for use in the guard
Guards make match a complete replacement for if/elif chains
Order matters: first matching arm with a true guard wins
Use guards for conditions that can't be expressed as simple patterns
common_mistakes: Writing the guard condition before the `if` keyword
Forgetting the pattern variable: `if x > 10` needs `n if n > 10`
Putting a generic pattern before a guarded one — the generic one captures first
